title: Retail Installment Contracts Servicing Standard: Spacing Allowance Between Hardship Extensions
content:
**Standard.** The spacing allowance for a hardship extension agreement on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts is set by when the contract's latest extension took effect, measured back from the signing date:

- when the contract has no earlier extension, or its latest extension took effect on or before the same calendar day **24** months before the signing date, the allowance is the tier's maximum installments deferred by one extension;
- when the latest extension took effect later than the same calendar day **12** months before the signing date, the allowance is zero;
- in between, it is **one** installment.

Where the same calendar day does not exist in the month counted back to, the last day of that month is used, for both the 24-month and the 12-month marks.

## Boundary table (hypothetical signing date of 15 September)

| Latest extension took effect | Spacing allowance |
|---|---|
| none ever | the tier's per-request maximum |
| 15 September, two years earlier | the tier's per-request maximum (on the 24-month mark) |
| 16 September, two years earlier | one installment |
| 15 September, one year earlier | one installment (on the 12-month mark, not later than it) |
| 16 September, one year earlier | zero |

**Month-end case.** Signing on 31 August: the 12-month mark is 31 August of the year before, the 24-month mark 31 August two years before. Signing on 29 February: the marks fall on 28 February one and two years before, those years having no 29 February.
